questions.q: What is an architecture decision record (ADR), as used in this lesson's write-up prompt?
options: A log file automatically generated by Kubernetes
A short written format that captures why a decision was made, not just what the decision was
A type of Prometheus alert rule
A certificate awarded for completing the capstone
questions.explain: An ADR's purpose is to record the reasoning behind a decision, which is why the write-up asks 'what would break first and why,' not just 'what would you change.'

questions.q: At 10x the capstone's scale, which two course concepts does the lesson suggest re-examining first?
options: The programming language used and the GPU brand
Storage choice (direct S3 reads vs. a cached parallel filesystem) and checkpoint frequency
The color scheme of the monitoring dashboard
The capstone's internet connection speed
questions.explain: The 10x prompt specifically asks whether the storage approach from Chapter 5 and checkpoint frequency ideas from Chapter 4 would still hold up at a larger size.

questions.q: According to the course recap, what does Chapter 4 of Distributed Training Infrastructure cover?
options: Networking and NCCL collective communication
Fault tolerance: checkpoint storage strategies, resuming large jobs, and designing for node failure
GPU utilization monitoring with DCGM
Kubernetes job scheduling basics
questions.explain: Chapter 4, 'Fault Tolerance & Checkpointing at Scale,' covers why long runs need fault tolerance, checkpoint storage, resuming, and designing for node failure.

questions.q: What is the relationship between Distributed Training Infrastructure and Advanced LLM Training & ML Systems, as described in this lesson?
options: They cover the exact same material in a different order
This course covers the infrastructure underneath a training run; the next course covers the training algorithms that run on top of it
Advanced LLM Training & ML Systems is a prerequisite for this course
They are unrelated courses in different career paths
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames this course as staying on the infrastructure side of the Chapter 1 split, with Advanced LLM Training & ML Systems picking up the algorithm side.

questions.q: Why does the lesson suggest including a sentence about anything that didn't work the first time in the capstone?
options: Because a perfect first attempt disqualifies the write-up
Because debugging a real distributed setup, even a small one, is the actual skill the course has been building
Because instructors require a minimum number of bugs to be reported
Because failed attempts are not relevant to a technical write-up
questions.explain: The lesson frames troubleshooting (e.g. a misconfigured replica spec or checkpoint path) as part of the genuine skill being practiced, worth documenting rather than omitting.
